issues.legal_issue: A claimant relying on a registered sale deed and evidence of means to purchase property establishes ownership against an attachment for a spouse’s debt when the attaching creditor neither clearly pleads nor proves that the spouse was the real purchaser.
material_facts: The property was attached in proceedings to recover sums owed to the claimant’s husband, and the claimant sued to have it released as her personal property.
The claimant produced a duly executed registered sale deed in her favor and oral and documentary evidence of her income and other means to pay the purchase price.

The attaching creditor did not clearly plead that the husband had purchased the property benami in the claimant’s name and produced no evidence that he paid the consideration, held the deed, possessed the property, or had a motive for the transaction.
The trial court found that the claimant owned the property, but the High Court reversed without properly assessing the evidence and placed the burden on the claimant to prove she was the real owner.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s ownership was established and the attachment could not stand; the appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the suit was decreed.
issues.legal_principle: A duly executed registered sale deed is evidence of the claimant’s title. Where the claimant also explains her means to pay the purchase price, the burden rests on the party asserting that the transaction was benami to prove that the apparent ownership is not the real ownership. Relevant evidence may include who paid the consideration, who held the deed, who possessed the property, and the motive for the transaction. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: appeal_in_property_release_suit and registered_deed_in_claimants_favour and claimant_evidence_of_purchase_means and creditor_did_not_plead_benami and creditor_lacks_benami_evidence

predicates.appeal_in_property_release_suit: The proceeding was an appeal in a civil suit seeking release of property attached for a debt owed by the claimant’s spouse.
predicates.registered_deed_in_claimants_favour: The claimant relied on a duly executed registered sale deed in her favor for the property.
predicates.claimant_evidence_of_purchase_means: The claimant gave oral or documentary evidence of having means to pay the purchase price.
predicates.creditor_did_not_plead_benami: The creditor seeking to enforce the attachment did not clearly plead that the spouse purchased the property benami in the claimant’s name.
predicates.creditor_lacks_benami_evidence: The creditor produced no evidence that the spouse paid the consideration, held the deed, possessed the property, or had a motive for the transaction.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a suit to release property attached for a spouse’s debt, a registered deed and the claimant’s evidence of means to purchase establish the claimant’s ownership against the attachment if the creditor neither clearly pleaded benami ownership nor produced evidence supporting it.
